𝗧𝗿𝗮𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰 𝗔𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿𝘆 𝗳𝗼𝗿 (𝗝𝘂𝗺𝗺𝗮𝘁-𝗨𝗹-𝗩𝗶𝗱𝗮) 𝗟𝗮𝘀𝘁 𝗙𝗿𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘆 𝗣𝗿𝗮𝘆𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗼𝗳 𝗥𝗮𝗺𝘇𝗮𝗻 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗵 𝗼𝗻 𝟮𝟬.𝟬𝟯.𝟮𝟬𝟮𝟲 𝗜𝗻 𝗛𝘆𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗯𝗮𝗱.

In connection with JUMMAT-UL-VIDA (last Friday of Ramzan month) prayers at Mecca Masjid, Charminar, the main roads from Charminar towards Madina, Murgi chowk and Shalibanda will be closed for all types of vehicular traffic from 0800 hours to 1600 hours on 20-03-2026. Traffic will be diverted at the following points:-

A. Charminar Zone: 

1.MADINA JUNCTION:- The traffic coming from the Nayapul side towards the Charminar will be diverted at Madina junction towards City College.
2. HIMMATPURA:- The Traffic coming from the Nagulchintha / Shalibanda areas towards Charminar will be diverted at Himmatpura Junction, towards Hari Bowli and Volga Hotel T Junction (Khilwat side).
3. CHOWK MAIDAN KAMAN:- The Traffic coming from the Chowk Maidan towards Charminar will be diverted towards  Kotla  Aliza or Moghalpura Sides.
4. MOTIGALLI:- The Traffic coming from the Moosabowli areas towards Charminar, and it will be diverted at Motigalli towards Khilwath ground , Rajesh Medical Hall Shalibanda, and Fathe Darwaza Road
5. ETEBAR CHOWK:- The Traffic coming from the Etebar Chowk areas towards Gulzarhouse will be diverted at  Etebar Chowk, towards Mandi Miralam Market or Bibi Bazar.
6. SHER E BATIL KAMAN:- The Traffic coming from Mitti Ka Sher will not be allowed towards Gulzar House and it will be diverted from Mitti-ke-Sher Junction towards Ghansi Bazaar to reach High court road / Khilwath.
7.LAKKAD KOTE (OLD CP OFFICE JUNCTION) The traffic coming from APAT side will be diverted at Lakkad Kote and sent towards (Old CP Office lane), towards Mandi Mirlam Market. (need basis)

Parking Places in The Limits of Traffic South Zone:

1.Gulzar Function Hall: The devotees coming from Madina, Pathargatti, will park their vehicles at Gulzar Function Hall (The Inspector of Traffic PS Mirchowk has to make arrangement for parking in this function hall).
2. Mufeed ul Anam Ground parking: The devotees who are coming from Yakuthpura- Noorkhan Bazar, Talab katta and Dabeerpura will park their vehicles at Mufid Ul Anam Grounds. (The Inspector of Traffic PS. Mirchowk has to make arrangement for parking in this ground).
3. Charminar Bus terminal parking:  The Devotees coming from Chandrayangutta and Falaknuma areas will park their vehicles at Charminar Bus terminal. (The Inspector of Tr. PS. Charminar will look after this parking).
4. A.U Hospital Parking: The devotees coming from Santosh Nagar Talab Katta Moghalpura will park their vehicles at AU Hospital parking. (The Inspector Tr PS. Charminar will look after this parking).
5. Khilwat Ground parking: The Devotees coming from Misrigunj, Fathe Darwaza, Hussaini alam and Puranapool sides will park their vehicles at Khilwat Ground. (The Inspector Tr. PS. Falaknuma will look after this parking)
6. Old Pension office / URDU Maskan Opp: Chowmohalla Palace: The traffic coming from the western side of the Mecca Masjid i.e., Kishanbagh Bahadurpura Hussanui Alam will park their vehicles at the above mention parking places. (The Inspector Tr. PS. Charminar will look after this parking).

These restrictions apply to the RTC buses also. City Buses going towards Charminar will be terminated at Afzalgunj Bus Stop. RTC buses going to districts via Nayapool, Madina from MGBS, Imlibun will proceed via: Chadarghat Rotary Nalgonda X – Chanchalguda – Saidabad T Junction - I.S Sadan – DMRL Junction – Midhani Junction – MBNR Fly over – Bandlaguda – towards Aramghar.

B. Secunderabad Zone: 

1.The Subhash Road in Secunderabad (between Mahankali L&O PS and Old Ramgopalpet PS Junction on the MG road) will be closed for vehicular traffic from 9.00 a.m. to 1.p.m. Traffic will be diverted Rocha Bazar towards Ranigunj and Paradise junction.
2. Traffic coming from Bata X Roads towards Subhash Road will be diverted at Mahankali L&O P.S. towards the lane to the left of the Mahankali L&O P.S. and towards Lala temple.

Commuters are requested  to follow the traffic updates on our social media platform @ https://t.co/i8FADg99rF HYDTP and X https://t.co/3pPxhN11AT HYDTP. In case of emergency, the commuters are requested to call our traffic help line 9010203626 for any travel assistance and cooperate with the Hyderabad Traffic Police.     
 
 Jt. Commissioner of Police,
Traffic, Hyderabad City.

Thursday Wheat Report
Thursday, March 19, 2026

The wheat market is surging to nine-month highs this Thursday as a "perfect storm" of geopolitical chaos and environmental degradation hits the complex. With crude oil breaching the $120 mark due to the escalating Strait of Hormuz blockade, wheat has transitioned from a seasonal commodity into a high-priority food security hedge. The focus has shifted violently from "record global supplies" to "unaffordable logistics" and "collapsing U.S. yields," triggering a wave of speculative buying not seen in nearly two years.

Futures & Market News

Wheat futures are exploding today, led by Kansas City (HRW) as traders price in an 11th-hour crisis for the U.S. Southern Plains. The 21-day correlation between Kansas Wheat and Crude Oil has reached a staggering 98%.

May 2026 (K): $6.26 1/4 (+19 1/4)

July 2026 (N): $6.38 3/4 (+18 1/2)

September 2026 (U): $6.51 1/2 (+17 3/4)

December 2026 (Z): $6.69 0/4 (+16 1/2)

Key Driver: The "Agriflation" Spike. Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has essentially frozen a fifth of the world's oil supply, sending fuel and nitrogen fertilizer (Urea) costs to record levels. Wheat is being used as the primary vehicle for investors to play this inflationary cycle, as shipping insurance for Black Sea and Gulf exports continues to skyrocket.

USDA Wheat News: Weekly Export Sales

This morning's USDA report confirmed that international buyers are panic-buying U.S. supplies before prices climb further:

Weekly Net Sales: Totaled 496,000 MT, coming in at the high end of trade expectations.

Top Buyers: Mexico remains the anchor (153k MT), followed by a significant purchase from the Philippines (147k MT). Taiwan also tendered for 105k MT of milling wheat this morning.

2026/27 New Crop: We saw a massive jump in new crop bookings (212,100 MT), signaling that global importers are no longer waiting for a "harvest dip" to secure their 2026 needs.

Pace: Total commitments are now 22% ahead of last year, far outpacing the USDA's projected growth.

Commitments of Traders: Managed Money
The "Short Eject Button" has been hit. Funds that were aggressively bearish in February are now caught in one of the sharpest rallies of the decade.

Net Position: Managed money has flipped from a heavy net short to a growing net long position over the last 72 hours.

Trend: Longs are "piling in" as wheat is increasingly viewed as a geopolitical hedge.

Sentiment: The market has moved into "overbought" territory technically, but with the Hormuz crisis unresolved, traditional indicators are being ignored in favor of macro-risk headlines.

Crop & Weather Update
Domestic (U.S. Plains): The situation is dire. A persistent La Niña pattern has left the Southern Plains—specifically Kansas, Oklahoma, and Texas—facing "hot, dry, and windy" conditions during the critical spring green-up.

Kansas Ratings: The Brugler500 index for Kansas dropped to 339, reflecting a 22% plunge in crop conditions this month.

International: Russia remains a structural cap on prices with projected March exports of 4.3 MMT, but logistics are slowing. Maersk and other major lines are now diverting vessels around the Cape of Good Hope, adding thousands of miles and massive freight surcharges to Black Sea grain.

Regional Cash Bids (HRW & SRW Averages)

Basis is holding steady as the rapid rise in futures has sidelined some commercial buyers, while producers have largely "shut the bin doors" hoping for $7.00.

Region Average Basis Average Cash Price

Central Kansas (HRW)-0.71 K$5.55 1/4

Eastern Nebraska (HRW)-0.92 K$5.34 1/4

Southern Illinois (SRW)-0.38 K$5.88 1/4

Pacific Northwest (White)+0.48 K$6.74 1/4

Summary & Strategies
Summary: We have moved beyond fundamental "supply and demand." This is a macro-risk event. Wheat is tracking Energy and Geopolitics. Until there is a ceasefire in the Middle East or a major rain event in Kansas, the path of least resistance remains higher.

Strategies:

Producers: We have surged past our $6.25 target for May. If you have 2026 New Crop (July/Sept) unpriced, you are now looking at $6.40 - $6.50. This is a "Black Swan" rally—don't get greedy. Lock in another 15-20% at these levels.

Commercials: Be wary of "delivered" prices. With the Strait of Hormuz closed, freight and fuel surcharges will be the dominant factor in your margins for the next 30 days.

Watch Point: Monitor the Monday Crop Progress report. If Kansas "Good/Excellent" ratings fall into the teens, expect another $0.20-0.30 leg up in the HRW contracts.
#wheat
